coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with four advisories. Twenty-four attacks run, none landed. Custody holds: subject 2f35a2e0 at 0444, 42145 bytes, unmoved and unedited, dispatch pin agreeing and no digest token unfilled; HEAD never left 5d5d778; file 08 equal to the subject's own pin; required-now 26 of 26 and condition 2 at 4 of 32 NOT MET. Nine of nine cited digests reproduce. This is a first-turn harness specification that already carries the repairs its siblings needed a second turn to land, and in two places it goes further than any of them. It reproduces the entire live register row as one joined string as well as every cell individually — a check that can only fail, and it passes. Its role axis is bound to D-002 admitted identities rather than to a chosen corpus, with the slice-1 population corroborated twice in COORDINATOR-DECISIONS by D-002's 'Language roles: TypeScript, alone' and D-007's '{TypeScript}' role list; that is the analogue of the undefined-domain gap that sank G07's first turn, and it is closed. I ran the test that rejected G07 and G18 — a member whose stated obligation is not covered by the bytes it retains — across all four file-02 standardized families, every limb of each, and all five must-nots, and every one has a named home: trust routed to G08, lifecycle to G18, doctor integration to the doctor surface cell, and broker bypass to EV-3 rather than dropped when EV-4's three slash-joined limbs did not reach it. The punctuation discipline holds against everything I could construct: four semicolon members with the coordinating 'and' correctly identified as internal to the first field, one corpus class rather than eight because the live cell has no semicolon after the identifier sentence, eight surfaces in order, three executes limbs each witnessed by a named member through a per-member array I recomputed rather than trusted. The SARIF handling is the awkward part of this gate and it is right: the axis stays live, non-advertisement is recorded as testable content, advertisement-refusal goes to G26, optional advertised SARIF to DR-122, and file 01's historical DR-G17 mention is disclosed at the line where it sits rather than hoped past. One thing deserves separate notice. The candidate lands CLAUDE-V4-O1 — an advisory from the component-sdk-contract.v4 review observing that v4 named five Cancel-linearization traces and none for the two death-ordering branches — by naming drain-then-death-last and death-completes-T-5-without-restart in EV-3 and adding that observed process death is not a Cancel trigger. I read that observation rather than accepting the summary; the characterisation is exact. No dispatch asked for it. Four advisories, none blocking: OBL-G20-HARNESS-SPEC is coined here with no creating join and a gate-row home, now the third gate in that position after G07 and G18, which makes it a pattern worth a disposition rather than an oddity; gates2and3Hold is unscoped where DR-125 is plainly the row; bare NT identifiers are ambiguous against DR-131's own NT-5/6/7/8 sequence, with NT-7 naming two different classes at two different gates; and the two file-02 line ranges use different heading conventions, though both contain exactly what they claim. This ACCEPT does not close OBL-G20-HARNESS-SPEC; that additionally requires your recording.
